- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day windows.
- Underestimate late in the horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history is all zero (no market sentiment signal), assume no directional bias and apply mean reversion to recent 10-day average.
- Avoid sharp upward revisions after a 30-day forecast peak; cap forecast at 10% below the 30-day high if sentiment remains flat.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% for subsequent days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5 days are consistently above true outcome, reduce forecast by 1–1.5% per day starting from day 6.
